text:
maria: Heads up — saw a spike in east-west p99 latency and packet reordering for GPU pods in west1 after last night's hybrid CNI roll (Calico dataplane + Cilium 1.22 dataplane mode). Not a full outage but batching jobs failing with OOM/retries. :eyes:

anand: Confirming. Alerting showed retransmits up ~8x on the GPU node fleet. Started ~01:12 UTC when the calico-calicoctl daemonset restarted during the rollout.

jen: Which nodes? Is it all AZs in west1 or just the ones on our new MTU 9000 config?

maria: Primarily on the newer n2-gpu nodes in west1-a and west1-b. Older nodes (mtu 1500) look fine. Looks correlated with jumbo frame MTU=9000.

alex: Could be GSO/GRO interaction between Calico encapsulation and Cilium's host-repair path. I saw similar behavior when vxlan/geneve was mixed with direct routing — packets got re-ordered when offloads were enabled.

kai: Quick data: ran iperf between two GPU pods (same node vs cross node)

kai: ```
kai: # same-node (ok)
kai: iperf3 -c 10.4.3.12 -t 10
kai: [SUM]  0.00-10.00  sec  9.28 GBytes  7.87 Gbits/sec  sender
kai: 
kai: # cross-node (reordering, retransmits)
kai: iperf3 -c 10.4.5.23 -t 10
kai: Retransmits: 1800, jitter spikes, throughput drops to 1.2 Gbits/sec
kai: ```

anand: Also captured tcpdump on node nic when reproducing — I see large segments split and then arriving out of order. Snippet:

anand: ```
anand: 14:22:10.123456 IP 10.4.5.23.60000 > 10.4.3.12.5000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:22345, ack 9876, win 29200, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 1234567 ecr 7654321], length 10000
anand: 14:22:10.123460 IP 10.4.5.23.60000 > 10.4.3.12.5000: Flags [.], seq 22345:32345, ack 9876, length 10000
anand: ```

jen: That looks like offload/segmentation happening (10k length segments). What do ethtool and offload settings show?

alex: Ran ethtool -k on one affected NIC: GSO, GRO, TSO all on. Changing them to off reduced reordering but throughput tanked.

alex: ```
alex: # on affected node
alex: ethtool -k eth0
alex: tx-checksumming: on
alex: tx-checksum-ipv4: on
alex: tcp-segmentation-offload: on
alex: generic-segmentation-offload: on
alex: generic-receive-offload: on
alex: ```

maria: Related: our Cilium dataplane was upgraded to 1.22 and we enabled host-repair + masquerade. Calico is on as our network policy + IPAM overlay for some node groups — hybrid mode. Might be the encapsulation path and MTU mismatch causing fragments to get reassembled in wrong order.

ops-oncall: deploy-bot reports: "cni-rollout: calico-daemonset restarted 01:10 UTC, cilium-operator updated 01:11 UTC". No errors in the operator logs immediately but kube-proxy churn increased.

deploy-bot: cni-rollout: automated canary step rolled to 20% at 01:05, 50% at 01:09, 100% at 01:11. Rollback flag not set. :warning:

anand: Can we pin to calico 3.25 policy-only mode on the affected nodes and disable encapsulation temporarily? That would remove one path for segmentation changes.

jen: We can try. Quick mitigation plan: 1) set Calico to IPIP/None (policy-only) on canary subset 2) disable GSO/GRO on one node to validate 3) roll back Cilium dataplane to 1.21 if mitigation fails.

kai: I applied iptables rule to force packets through non-encap path for one pod pair (policy tweak). Saw retransmits drop ~70% in 5m.

maria: Nice. Can we schedule a rolling change to mark the rest of the new nodes as policy-only? Need change window and risk assessment.

alex: Before broader change, we should run a controlled A/B test: disable offloads on a node, toggle calico encapsulation, measure p99 and retransmits. I can script the test.

jen: I'll open a RFC and schedule a 60m window this afternoon. Risk: performance drop for high-throughput intra-node comms if we disable offloads permanently.

anand: Also let's capture RDMA logs — our RDMA L2 handshake lm logs show a few link resets around the same time. Might be NIC firmware and big MTU interplay with offload.

kai: grabbed dmesg from one node: 
kai: ```
kai: [   82.123456] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: NIC Link down
kai: [   83.234567] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: NIC Link up
kai: [   83.234789] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: mlx5: Intriguing: GSO/LSO data path mismatch
kai: ```

maria: OK. Immediate action: disable calico encapsulation on new-node pool (west1-a/b new-n2-gpu) to policy-only, and mark them drained for non-urgent batch work. Alex, Kai — run the A/B and report metrics in #eng-infra-runs.

alex: On it. Running script now. Test plan: 10k-packet streams across 10 pod pairs, measure retransmits/jitter/p99.

ops-oncall: I'm adding incident note and will keep watchers updated. If rollback to cilium 1.21 is needed we'll coordinate with release to avoid controller drift.

jen: If we rollback Cilium, we must also consider the policy CRDs introduced in 1.22 — there might be mismatch in kube-apiserver cache. We'll stage rollback to canary first.

maria: Thank you all. Please post short results here. If mitigation stabilizes, we'll schedule a full node-pool change and follow up with vendor (Mellanox) about firmware and offload interaction. :thumbsup:

alex: Preliminary A/B results (15m): encapsulation=on, offloads=on -> retransmits 1600 avg. encapsulation=off, offloads=on -> retransmits 420 avg. encapsulation=off, offloads=off -> retransmits 80 avg but throughput fell 40%.

kai: So looks like encapsulation + offloads amplifies reordering. Encapsulation off helps a lot.

anand: Filing ticket INF-4821 to track follow-ups: firmware check, calico config change, Cilium rollback plan, and long-term fix.

maria: Closing loop: mitigated by toggling calico to policy-only on affected nodes. We'll keep this thread open for post-mortem notes. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
